html:
The Spanish conquest of Nicaragua began with the expedition of Gil González Dávila in 1522, who met the ruler Nicarao, after whom the country is named. In 1524 Francisco Hernández de Córdoba founded the towns of Granada and León.

The Pacific lowlands held dense populations of farmers, among them the Nahua-speaking Nicarao. The Spanish fought them and among themselves, and governors such as Pedrarias Dávila had rivals beheaded.

The worst blow was a slave trade. Tens of thousands of Indigenous people, perhaps far more, were shipped to Panama and to Peru after the conquest of the Inca Empire. With disease, it emptied much of the lowlands. The Caribbean coast stayed outside Spanish control and later became the Mosquito Coast. León Viejo is the ruin of the first capital of Nicaragua.
